1. Calculate the moles of each reagent.  
   • CH₃COOH: 0.1 M × 0.500 L = 0.050 mol  
   • HCl:   0.2 M × 0.400 L = 0.080 mol (strong acid → 0.080 mol H⁺)  
   • Ba(OH)₂: 0.3 M × 0.300 L = 0.090 mol  
     Ba(OH)₂ furnishes 2 OH⁻ per formula unit → 0.090 mol × 2 = 0.180 mol OH⁻

2. Neutralize strong acid first.  
   OH⁻ available = 0.180 mol  
   H⁺ (from HCl)  = 0.080 mol  
   Remaining OH⁻ after neutralising HCl: 0.180 – 0.080 = 0.100 mol

3. Neutralize the weak acid (acetic acid).  
   CH₃COOH + OH⁻ → CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O  
   CH₃COOH present = 0.050 mol  
   It consumes an equal amount of OH⁻, leaving  
   Remaining OH⁻ = 0.100 – 0.050 = 0.050 mol  
   CH₃COO⁻ produced = 0.050 mol

4. Calculate [OH⁻] from the excess strong base (the hydrolysis of CH₃COO⁻ adds a negligible extra amount compared with the strong base already present).  
   Total volume = 0.500 L + 0.400 L + 0.300 L = 1.200 L  
   [OH⁻] = 0.050 mol / 1.200 L = 0.0417 M

5. Compute pOH and pH.  
   pOH = –log(0.0417) ≈ 1.38  
   pH  = 14 – pOH ≈ 14 – 1.38 = 12.62

Hence the solution is strongly basic.

Answer: C
